mainTopic: How the חכמים stopped חנינא's breakaway calendar in בבל, followed by the talks at יבנה in honor of Torah and in honor of those who host תלמידי חכמים.
overview: This amud opens at the end of the story of חנינא, the nephew of רבי יהושע, who began fixing the calendar on his own in בבל. The חכמים of ארץ ישראל warn the Jews of בבל that breaking away is like denying the God of Israel. The people cry out that they will stay loyal. The גמרא explains the harsh steps with the פסוק 'כי מציון תצא תורה'. It also explains why the scholars could overturn his strict rulings: they did it so people would stop following him. Next comes a ברייתא about the חכמים gathered in the כרם ביבנה. רבי יהודה speaks in honor of Torah. His talk covers the אהל outside the camp, משה returning to the people, the idea that Torah should feel new every day, and three readings of 'הסכת': learn in groups, wear yourself out for Torah, and absorb first, then analyze. Related teachings praise effort and humility in learning. Then רבי נחמיה, רבי יוסי and רבי אליעזר each use a קל וחומר to praise those who host a תלמיד חכם. The amud ends with עובד אדום's blessing of many children, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The warning message sent to the Jews of Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of ארץ ישראל tell the Jews of בבל: obey us, or it is as if you are setting up your own religion and denying the God of Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And tell our brothers in exile: if they listen, good. If not, let them go up a mountain. אחיה will build an altar, חנניה will play the lyre, and they will all deny God and say they have no portion in the God of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The חכמים send a sharp message to בבל warning that following חנינא's separate calendar is like breaking away from the Jewish people altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The message is sarcastic and meant to shock. Building a private altar outside the בית המקדש is like what ירבעם did when he split off from Jerusalem. The point is that setting up your own calendar away from ארץ ישראל is just as much a break from the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: The exile, meaning the Jewish community outside ארץ ישראל (here, בבל)
A lyre or harp, played by the לויים during the עבודה
They will deny God, become heretics
A portion in the God of Israel

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not actually telling anyone to build an altar or deny God. It is a rhetorical threat. They are showing where breaking away from ארץ ישראל leads.

phrases.english: And tell our brothers who are in the exile:
If they listen, good;
and if not, let them go up onto a mountain,
Achiya will build an altar,
phrases.notes: אחיה was one of the leaders of the Babylonian community.

phrases.english: Chananya will play the lyre,
phrases.notes: חנניה was a לוי, so he is cast in the role of the Temple musician.

phrases.english: and they will all deny God,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֹאמְרוּ אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק בֵּאלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: and they will say they have no portion in the God of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִמְרוּ לְאַחֵינוּ שֶׁבַּגּוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun earlier on the daf, about the scholars sent to oppose חנינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking away from the authority of ארץ ישראל on the calendar is framed as equal to leaving the God of Israel.

steps.title: The people cry and refuse to break away
steps.stepSummary: Hearing the message, the whole nation cries and declares that they do have a portion in the God of Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately all the people burst into tears and said: God forbid! We do have a portion in the God of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its climax. The warning works, and the people reject the idea of breaking away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crying shows the people never meant to leave Judaism. Once they saw that a separate calendar meant splitting from the nation, they backed down and stayed loyal to ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: The story ends with the Babylonian community choosing to stay connected to the authority of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Immediately all the people burst out crying
and they said: God forbid!
We do have a portion in the God of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד גָּעוּ כׇּל הָעָם בִּבְכִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the people's reaction to the warning in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people reject breaking away and affirm their bond with the God of Israel.

steps.title: Why go to such extremes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים took such drastic steps to stop חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the story and asks a question. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנינא was a great scholar, and fixing the calendar is a מצוה. So it seems surprising that the חכמים would humiliate him and threaten the whole community. The גמרא wants to know what justified this.

keyTerms.meaning: And why all this? Why go so far?

phrases.english: And why all this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל כָּךְ לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reason behind the actions described in the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What justified such extreme measures against חנינא and the Babylonian community?

steps.title: Torah must come from Zion
steps.stepSummary: The answer is a פסוק: Torah goes out from ציון and the word of ה׳ from ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says: 'For out of Zion shall go forth Torah, and the word of ה׳ from Jerusalem.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a פסוק from ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that the center of Torah authority belongs in ארץ ישראל. Moving the calendar authority to בבל would weaken that center and could split the nation, so strong action was justified.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is stated (in a פסוק)
Zion, meaning ירושלים and ארץ ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the whole story. Keeping one central Torah authority, especially for the calendar that all Jews share, is so important that it overrides normal respect for an individual scholar.

phrases.english: Because it is stated:
'For out of Zion shall go forth Torah,'
phrases.notes: ישעיה ב:ג

phrases.english: 'and the word of ה׳ from Jerusalem.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Torah authority must come out of ארץ ישראל, as the פסוק 'כי מציון תצא תורה' says.

steps.title: How could they rule pure what he ruled impure?
steps.stepSummary: Ruling stricter than חנינא makes sense, but ruling טהור after he ruled טמא seems to break a ברייתא that forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense when he ruled pure and they ruled impure, since that is being strict. But when he ruled impure and they ruled pure, how could that be? Didn't a ברייתא teach: if a חכם ruled something impure, his colleague may not rule it pure; if he forbade it, his colleague may not permit it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier detail of the story, where the scholars contradicted חנינא in both directions. It challenges the case where they were more lenient than he was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being stricter than another חכם is not a problem, because nothing is lost by being careful. But a ברייתא says that once one חכם rules something טמא or אסור, another חכם may not come and permit it. So how could the scholars overrule חנינא's strict rulings?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, granted (sets up a contrast with a harder case)
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא only forbids overriding a strict ruling to make it lenient. Overriding a lenient ruling to make it strict is fine, which is why the גמרא says the first case is no problem.

phrases.english: It makes sense where he ruled pure
and they ruled impure, since that is toward strictness.
But where he ruled impure and they ruled pure,
how could that be?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: חָכָם שֶׁטִּמֵּא — אֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְטַהֵר,
phrases.english: A Sage who ruled impure, his colleague is not allowed to rule pure;
if he forbade, his colleague is not allowed to permit!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הוּא מְטַהֵר, וְהֵם מְטַמְּאִין — לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to an earlier detail of the story (the scholars contradicting חנינא) and questions its legality.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scholars' practice of ruling טהור on things חנינא had ruled טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids a חכם from permitting what a colleague has already forbidden, so their lenient contradictions seem forbidden.

steps.title: They did it so people would not follow him
steps.stepSummary: The scholars deliberately overrode him so that the people would stop following חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They held that it was needed so that people would not be drawn after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The normal rule was set aside on purpose to undercut חנינא's authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is the normal rule. Here, however, there was an emergency: the unity of the nation was at risk. Showing that חנינא's rulings could be overturned stopped people from treating him as the final authority.

keyTerms.meaning: They held, they were of the opinion
So that ... not, in order that ... not
They will be drawn after him, follow him

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that one חכם may not permit what another forbade still stands. Here it was set aside because of an emergency, to protect the central authority of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבְרִי כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא נִגָּרְרוּ בָּתְרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: They held: so that people would not be drawn after him.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבְרִי כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא נִגָּרְרוּ בָּתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Emergency exception: the general rule is set aside for a pressing communal need.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scholars were simply breaking the ברייתא's rule against overriding a strict ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: They knowingly set the rule aside so that people would stop following חנינא, protecting the authority of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The חכמים gather in the כרם of יבנה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא sets the scene: four great sages were at the כרם ביבנה, and each opened his talk by honoring the hosts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When our Rabbis entered the vineyard in יבנה, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, רבי נחמיה, and רבי אליעזר the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי were there. They all opened their talks by honoring their hosts, and then they taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא that sets up a scene. It is preparing the next steps, where we hear what each sage actually taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'vineyard' (כרם) is a name for the study hall in יבנה, because the students sat in rows like vines. Each sage began by thanking the hosts. That was a sign of respect and gratitude toward the people who housed them and their students.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
The 'vineyard' in יבנה, a name for the great study hall there
Honor of the hosts, the people who give guests a place to stay
They opened, meaning they began their talk

steps.confusionAlert: The כרם is not a real vineyard with grapes here. It is the name of the study hall in יבנה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
When our Rabbis entered the vineyard (study hall) in Yavne,

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שָׁם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: there were there Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Nechemya and Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
They all opened in honor of the hosts, and taught.
phrases.notes: Each speech began by praising the hosts.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן כְּשֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ לַכֶּרֶם בְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא after the story of חנינא ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sages in יבנה opened their teachings by honoring their hosts.

steps.title: רבי יהודה opens with כבוד תורה and quotes the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה, the lead speaker, opened with כבוד תורה and quoted the פסוק about משה taking the אהל outside the camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, the head speaker everywhere, opened in honor of Torah and taught: 'And משה would take the tent and pitch it outside the camp.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה begins his talk by quoting a פסוק. This is the setup for the קל וחומר he is about to build in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Background: after the חטא העגל, משה moved the אהל outside the camp, and anyone who wanted ה׳ had to walk out to it. רבי יהודה, the ראש המדברים who always spoke first, uses that picture to praise people who go out of their way to learn Torah. Notice that step 7 said they all opened בכבוד אכסניא, but רבי יהודה opens בכבוד תורה. The talks in honor of the hosts come later, from רבי נחמיה, רבי יוסי and רבי אליעזר (steps 34-36).

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the speakers, the one who always spoke first
He taught by explaining a פסוק

phrases.aramaic: פָּתַח רַבִּי יְהוּדָה רֹאשׁ הַמְדַבְּרִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, the head of the speakers in every place, opened
in honor of Torah, and taught:
"And Moshe would take the tent
and pitch it outside the camp" (Shemos 33:7).
phrases.notes: This happened after the sin of the golden calf.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּתַח רַבִּי יְהוּדָה רֹאשׁ הַמְדַבְּרִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם בִּכְבוֹד תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Zooms in on one of the speakers from the scene in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה builds his talk in honor of Torah on the פסוק of משה's אהל outside the camp.

steps.title: Torah scholars who travel are true seekers of ה׳
steps.stepSummary: Using a קל וחומר, רבי יהודה proves that תלמידי חכמים who travel to learn are even more worthy of the title 'seekers of ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? The ארון of ה׳ was only twelve מיל away, and the Torah still said 'everyone who seeks ה׳ would go out to the אהל מועד.' Then תלמידי חכמים, who go from city to city and from country to country to learn Torah, are seekers of ה׳ all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה draws his lesson from the פסוק. He uses a קל וחומר to praise those who travel to learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small case is walking only twelve מיל to the אהל, and the Torah already calls that person a 'seeker of ה׳.' The bigger case is scholars who travel much greater distances to learn. They certainly deserve that title. This fits the setting, because the sages and students in יבנה were guests who had traveled to learn.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if a smaller case has a quality, a bigger case has it even more
A measure of distance, roughly a kilometer

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who travels to learn Torah is called a מבקש ה׳, a seeker of ה׳.

phrases.english: And are these words not a kal vachomer?

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אֲרוֹן ה׳ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מְרוּחָק
phrases.english: If regarding the Ark of ה׳, which was not far away
except twelve mil,
phrases.notes: The camp of Israel stretched twelve mil.

phrases.english: the Torah said: "And everyone who sought ה׳
would go out to the Tent of Meeting" —
Torah scholars who go from city to city
and from country to country to learn Torah,
how much more so (are they seekers of ה׳).

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא דְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the פסוק quoted in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That traveling תלמידי חכמים are called seekers of ה׳.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the פסוק calling those who walked twelve מיל to the אהל מועד 'seekers of ה׳.'

steps.title: ה׳ and משה will show a pleasant face in learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains 'face to face' to mean ה׳ told משה that they would both show a pleasant face in הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And ה׳ spoke to משה face to face.' רבי יצחק said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה: משה, you and I will show a pleasant face in הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק in the same section and brings רבי יצחק's explanation of 'face to face.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק reads 'face to face' as warmth, not only closeness. ה׳ and משה should both show a pleasant, welcoming face in Torah learning. This continues the theme of honoring Torah and the people who come to learn it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will show a pleasant, welcoming face

phrases.aramaic: ״וְדִבֶּר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה פָּנִים אֶל פָּנִים״,
phrases.english: "And ה׳ spoke to Moshe face to face" (Shemos 33:11).
Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:
Moshe, I and you
will show a pleasant face in halacha.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִבֶּר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה פָּנִים אֶל פָּנִים אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next פסוק in the same passage about the אהל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Face to face' teaches that ה׳ and משה show a pleasant face in Torah learning.

steps.title: Another version: show Israel a pleasant face and bring the tent back
steps.stepSummary: A second version (איכא דאמרי): ה׳ told משה to show Israel the same warmth ה׳ showed him, and to return the אהל to its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is what הקדוש ברוך הוא told משה: Just as I showed you a pleasant face, so you should show Israel a pleasant face, and bring the tent back to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רבי יצחק's teaching. This version adds a practical instruction for משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, ה׳ and משה together show warmth. In this version, ה׳'s warmth to משה is a model, and משה must pass it on to the people. Practically, that means ending the distance and bringing the אהל back into the camp.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; this introduces another version of a teaching
Return the tent to its place

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: Thus the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:
Just as I showed you a pleasant face,
so you show a pleasant face to Israel,
and return the tent to its place.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Alternative version of the same מימרא
steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי כָּךְ אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבי יצחק's teaching in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה must show Israel the warmth ה׳ showed him and bring the אהל back into the camp.

steps.title: If teacher and student are both angry, what will happen to Israel?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains 'and he returned to the camp': ה׳ told משה that if both of them stay angry, Israel is lost. So משה must bring the אהל back, or יהושע will lead in his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he returned to the camp.' רבי אבהו said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה: Now people will say, the Teacher is angry and the student is angry, so what will become of Israel? If you bring the tent back to its place, good. If not, יהושע בן נון your student will serve in your place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אבהו's explanation of why משה returned to the camp. ה׳ pushed משה to come back to the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה had moved away from the people because ה׳ was angry with them. רבי אבהו teaches that a leader must not copy the anger. If both the 'Teacher' (ה׳) and the 'student' (משה) are angry, no one is left to bring the people back. So ה׳ warned משה: return, or יהושע will take over your role.

keyTerms.meaning: And he returned to the camp

steps.whatToRemember: A Torah leader must stay close to the people and show them warmth, even when there is reason for anger.
steps.confusionAlert: 'The Teacher' (הרב) here means ה׳, and 'the student' (תלמיד) means משה.

phrases.english: "And he returned to the camp," etc. (Shemos 33:11).
Rabbi Abahu said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:

phrases.aramaic: עַכְשָׁיו יֹאמְרוּ הָרַב בְּכַעַס וְתַלְמִיד בְּכַעַס,
phrases.english: Now they will say: the Teacher is angry and the student is angry,
phrases.notes: The Teacher is ה׳; the student is משה.

phrases.english: what will become of Israel?

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה מַחֲזִיר הָאֹהֶל לִמְקוֹמוֹ — מוּטָב,
phrases.english: If you return the tent to its place, good;
and if not,

phrases.aramaic: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן תַּלְמִידְךָ מְשָׁרֵת תַּחְתֶּיךָ.
phrases.english: Yehoshua bin Nun, your student, will serve in your place.
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues: 'and his servant יהושע בן נון did not leave the tent.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁב אֶל הַמַּחֲנֶה וְגוֹ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of step 11 (bringing the אהל back) by explaining the next words of the פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the end of the פסוק, where יהושע stays in the אהל: he was ready to replace משה if משה did not return.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ required משה to return the אהל to the people, warning that otherwise יהושע would replace him.

steps.title: The verse that matches משה's return to the camp
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ties רבי אבהו's explanation to the פסוק 'ושב אל המחנה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is what is written: 'And he returned to the camp.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אבהו's teaching by pointing to the exact words in the פסוק that match it. משה listened to ה׳ and went back to the camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, רבי אבהו said ה׳ told משה to bring the אהל back. Here the גמרא shows the פסוק records that משה did exactly that. The words 'ושב אל המחנה' are the proof that משה obeyed.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is what is written: it links an idea to a פסוק
Camp: the camp of the Jewish people

phrases.english: And that is what is written:
"And he returned to the camp."
phrases.notes: שמות לג:יא

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אבהו's statement by quoting the matching פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's claim that משה brought the אהל back to the camp

steps.title: רבא: The warning about יהושע still came true
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even though משה went back, the words about יהושע were not wasted. יהושע stayed in the אהל and eventually took over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even so, the statement did not go out for nothing. As it says: 'And his servant יהושע בן נון, a young man, did not leave the tent.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds that ה׳'s warning ('יהושע will lead in your place') still had an effect, even though משה obeyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if משה obeyed, you might think the threat about יהושע was simply cancelled. רבא says no. The second half of the same פסוק shows that יהושע stayed in the אהל, and later he really did become the leader after משה.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not move away / did not leave

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying משה disobeyed. משה did return. Even so, יהושע's special place in the אהל, and his future leadership, remained.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even so,
the statement did not go out for nothing.
As it is said:
"And his servant, Yehoshua bin Nun, a young man,
did not leave from inside the tent."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a qualification: משה's return did not fully erase the warning about יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s words about יהושע were fulfilled: יהושע stayed in the אהל and eventually succeeded משה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה opens again with the פסוק 'Today you became a nation'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה begins a second teaching in honor of Torah and quotes the פסוק 'הסכת ושמע ישראל היום הזה נהיית לעם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה again opened in honor of Torah and taught: 'Be silent and listen, ישראל: today you have become a nation.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה starts a new speech in honor of Torah by quoting a פסוק. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words were said at the end of משה's life, 40 years after מתן תורה. The phrase 'היום הזה' (this day) sounds odd, and the גמרא is about to ask about it.

keyTerms.meaning: And he again opened (began a new speech)
Be silent / pay attention (later read as 'make groups')

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda again opened
in honor of Torah and expounded:
"Be silent and listen, Israel;
this day you have become a nation"
phrases.notes: דברים כז:ט

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד פָּתַח רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בִּכְבוֹד תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching by the same speaker from Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה presents the פסוק 'היום הזה נהיית לעם' as a source about honoring Torah.

steps.title: But the Torah was given forty years earlier
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asks, as part of his own דרשה: was the Torah given on that day? That day was at the end of 40 years in the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was the Torah given to ישראל on that day? Wasn't that day the end of forty years?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside his speech, רבי יהודה points out a problem with the פסוק. It says 'today you became a nation,' but the Torah was given 40 years before. The next step gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We became a nation through receiving the Torah at סיני. So why would משה say 'today' at the end of 40 years? The question forces us to find a deeper meaning in the word 'today.'

keyTerms.meaning: But is it so that...? (a surprised question)

phrases.english: But was it on that day
that the Torah was given to Israel?
But wasn't that day
at the end of forty years!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain meaning of 'היום הזה' in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'היום הזה' in דברים כז:ט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah was given at סיני 40 years earlier, so 'today' cannot literally be the day we became a nation.

steps.title: Torah should feel new every single day
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק teaches that Torah is as beloved to those who learn it every day as on the day it was given at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches you that the Torah is beloved to those who learn it, every single day, like the day it was given from Mount סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers his own question. 'Today' means that every day of learning should feel like מתן תורה all over again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'today' is not about the date. It describes how Torah feels to the one who learns it. To a real learner, Torah never gets old, and each day is like standing at סיני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for the idea that Torah learning should feel fresh and exciting every day, not old or routine.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to teach you
that the Torah is beloved to those who learn it
on each and every day
like the day it was given from Mount Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁחֲבִיבָה תּוֹרָה עַל לוֹמְדֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by reading 'today' as describing how Torah feels, not the date.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק's wording (non-literal reading of 'today')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Today' means the actual day the Torah was given, which does not fit the timeline.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Today' teaches that Torah is as beloved every day as on the day of מתן תורה.

steps.title: Proof from missing one קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום shows how precious daily Torah is: someone who skips קריאת שמע even once is like someone who never said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום son of רבי חייא, of the village of עכו, said: Know this. A person says קריאת שמע morning and night. If one evening he does not say it, he is like someone who never said קריאת שמע at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי תנחום brings a proof that each day of Torah counts as something new and precious. Missing even one day is a real loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Torah were 'old news,' missing one time would not matter much. But since each day is like a new מתן תורה, missing one evening is a loss that cannot be made up. This supports the idea from Step 17.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean his earlier קריאת שמע 'disappears' as a מצוה. It means each day's obligation is its own new thing, so missing one cannot be made up by all the other days.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum, son of Rabbi Chiya, said
a man of the village of Akko:
Know this —
for a person recites Shema
morning and evening,
and one evening he does not recite it —
he is like one who never recited
Shema ever.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּדַע — שֶׁהֲרֵי אָדָם קוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 17's teaching with a real-life example.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that Torah is new and beloved every single day
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of קריאת שמע: missing one evening is like never having said it

steps.title: 'הסכת' means: make groups to learn Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'הסכת' as 'עשו כתות' (make groups), teaching that Torah is only acquired by learning together.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'הסכת': Make many groups and learn Torah, because Torah is only acquired in a group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the word 'הסכת' from the פסוק and reads it as a hint: 'עשו כת' (make a group). The lesson is to learn Torah with others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הסכת is split into עשו (make) and כת (group). The reason given is that real Torah understanding only comes through learning with others, who can question and sharpen you.

keyTerms.meaning: Be busy with Torah, learn Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a central source for learning בחבורה or with a חברותא instead of alone.

phrases.english: "Hasket" —
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads הסכת as two words, עשו כת: 'make a group.'

phrases.english: make many groups
and engage in Torah.
Because the Torah is not acquired
except in a group.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הַסְכֵּת״ — עֲשׂוּ כִּתּוֹת כִּתּוֹת וְעִסְקוּ בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the same פסוק and explains a different word, הסכת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah is only truly acquired by learning in a group.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: A sword on those who learn alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads 'חרב אל הבדים' as a warning against תלמידי חכמים who learn alone (בד בבד).
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who said: What does the פסוק mean, 'A sword on the בדים, and they will become foolish'? A sword on the 'enemies' of תלמידי חכמים who sit alone, each by himself, and learn Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the idea of learning in groups with a teaching from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. He reads the word 'בדים' as 'בד בבד', people sitting alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בדים' is read as people who learn by themselves, alone. The פסוק threatens them with a 'sword,' which shows how serious it is to learn alone. 'Their enemies' is a polite way to say the תלמידי חכמים themselves, so the curse is not spoken directly about them.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the view of Rabbi...
Their enemies (a polite way to refer to the scholars themselves)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Enemies of תלמידי חכמים' is a respectful way of speaking. It really means the תלמידי חכמים themselves who learn alone, not actual enemies.

phrases.english: In line with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina,
for Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"A sword upon the baddim, and they shall become foolish" —
phrases.notes: ירמיהו נ:לו

phrases.english: a sword upon the enemies
of Torah scholars
who sit alone, each by himself
and engage in Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for Step 19's claim that Torah must be learned in a group.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו נ:לו, 'חרב אל הבדים', read as a sword on those who learn בד בבד

steps.title: Learning alone makes one foolish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי adds that people who learn alone become foolish, comparing 'ונאלו' to 'אשר נואלנו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but they become foolish. It is written here 'ונאלו,' and it is written there 'אשר נואלנו.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי continues: learning alone does more than bring danger. It also makes a person foolish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He compares the word 'ונאלו' in ירמיהו to 'נואלנו' in במדבר יב:יא, where אהרן says 'we acted foolishly.' Since the same root means foolishness there, it means foolishness here too. Without others to correct him, a lone learner can reach wrong conclusions.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also...
It is written here... and it is written there (comparing words in two פסוקים)

phrases.english: And not only that, but they become foolish,
it is written here "and they shall become foolish (noalu),"
and it is written there "that we have acted foolishly (noalnu)."
phrases.notes: במדבר יב:יא

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּטַּפְּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second harm of learning alone, proven by comparing words.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Word comparison: 'ונאלו' (ירמיהו נ:לו) with 'אשר נואלנו' (במדבר יב:יא)

steps.title: Learning alone even leads to sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי concludes that those who learn alone also come to sin, from the end of the same פסוק: 'ואשר חטאנו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but they sin, as it says: 'and that we have sinned.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds a final, more serious step: learning alone can lead a person to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in במדבר continues right after 'נואלנו' with 'ואשר חטאנו.' This shows that foolishness leads to sin. Someone who learns alone may get the הלכה wrong and then act on that mistake.
steps.whatToRemember: Torah should feel as fresh as at סיני every day, and it must be learned in a group. Learning alone is dangerous: it leads to foolishness, and foolishness leads to sin.

phrases.english: And not only that, but they sin,
as it is said: "and that we have sinned."
phrases.notes: End of במדבר יב:יא

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁחוֹטְאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the chain one step further: foolishness leads to sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuation of במדבר יב:יא: 'ואשר חטאנו'

steps.title: A second verse showing 'נואלו' means foolish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another פסוק to prove that people who learn alone become foolish: 'נואלו שרי צען.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you prefer, prove it from here: 'The princes of צען have become fools.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second source for the idea in Step 21 that 'ונאלו' means 'they become foolish.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 21, רבי יוסי proved the meaning of 'ונאלו' from 'אשר נואלנו.' Here the גמרא offers another פסוק where the same root clearly means foolishness: the princes of צען (Egypt's wise advisors) 'נואלו', meaning they became fools. The conclusion stays the same. Only the proof-text changes.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (introduces an alternative proof or answer)
צען, a city in מצרים known for its wise advisors

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is derived from here:
'The princes of Tzoan have become fools.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו יט:יג

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides an alternative proof-text for the meaning of 'ונאלו' from Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That 'ונאלו' means becoming foolish, so those who learn alone become fools.

steps.title: Second reading of 'הסכת': break yourselves over Torah
steps.stepSummary: A new interpretation reads 'הסכת' as 'כתתו עצמכם', meaning break or crush yourselves over Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Be silent and hear, Israel.' This means: crush yourselves over the words of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק 'הסכת ושמע ישראל' and gives it a new meaning: put yourself through effort and struggle for Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 19), 'הסכת' was split into 'עשו כתות', meaning make groups. Now the same letters are read as 'כתתו', from the root כתת, meaning to crush or grind. The lesson moves from learning with others to wearing yourself out for Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation (an alternative reading of the same verse)
Pay attention / be silent (the word being interpreted)

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'Keep silence and hear, Israel'
Break yourselves over the words of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: הַסְכֵּת וּשְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the פסוק from Step 19 and offers a different דרשה of 'הסכת.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must exert and 'crush' oneself for Torah.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Torah stays only with one who 'kills himself' over it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the 'crush yourself' reading with ריש לקיש's teaching from 'אדם כי ימות באהל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what ריש לקיש said. ריש לקיש said: How do we know that Torah stays only with a person who 'kills himself' over it? Because the פסוק says: 'This is the Torah: when a man dies in a tent.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the new reading in Step 24 fits a known teaching of ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in במדבר is really about טומאת מת in a tent. ריש לקיש reads it as a hint: 'This is the Torah' belongs to 'a man who dies in the tent', meaning someone who gives himself over completely in the tent of learning. This is the same idea as 'crush yourselves' over Torah.
steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not telling anyone to harm himself. 'Killing oneself' over Torah is a picture of total dedication and giving up comforts for learning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for the idea that real Torah knowledge stays only with someone who devotes himself to it completely.

phrases.english: As Reish Lakish said,
for Reish Lakish said:
From where do we know that words of Torah are not retained
except by one who kills himself over it?
As it is said:
'This is the Torah: when a man dies in a tent.'
phrases.notes: במדבר יט:יד

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading in Step 24 with a parallel teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That Torah requires total self-sacrifice ('כתתו עצמכם').
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's דרשה on 'זאת התורה אדם כי ימות באהל'

steps.title: Third reading of 'הסכת': first be quiet, then analyze
steps.stepSummary: Another reading splits 'הסכת' into 'הס' (be silent) and 'כתת' (grind, analyze): first absorb, then analyze.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Keep silence and hear, Israel.' This means: be quiet first, and afterwards analyze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third reading of 'הסכת' that teaches the right order of learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is split into two parts: 'הס', be silent and listen, and 'כתת', grind the material finely, meaning analyze it. The lesson is about order: first take in the material quietly, and only then break it down.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'Keep silence and hear, Israel'
Be silent, and afterwards analyze.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: הַסְכֵּת וּשְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative דרשה of the same word 'הסכת.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First absorb Torah quietly, then analyze it.

steps.title: רבא: learn first, then think deeply
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the 'be quiet, then analyze' reading with רבא's rule: learn Torah first, then reason it through.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches רבא. רבא said: A person should always learn Torah first, and afterwards think it through deeply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the reading in Step 26 fits רבא's well-known rule about the order of learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says to first build up knowledge (ילמוד), and only then analyze and reason (יהגה). This matches 'הס ואחר כך כתת' exactly: gather the material first, then dig into it.
steps.whatToRemember: The three readings of 'הסכת': (1) make groups and learn together; (2) crush yourself for Torah (ריש לקיש); (3) first absorb, then analyze (רבא).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's rule is a classic guide for how to learn: build knowledge first, and do deep analysis after.

phrases.english: As Rava, for Rava said:
A person should always learn Torah,
and afterwards analyze it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרָבָא, דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading in Step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That one should first absorb Torah and then analyze it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's rule: 'לעולם ילמוד אדם תורה ואחר כך יהגה'

steps.title: דבי רבי ינאי ask about the verse of milk, nose, and anger
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי opens a new teaching by asking what the פסוק in משלי about pressing milk, nose, and anger means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: What does the פסוק mean: 'For pressing milk brings out butter, pressing the nose brings out blood, and pressing anger brings out strife'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא opens a new teaching by quoting a פסוק and asking what it means, and the explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מאי דכתיב' tells us a new דרשה is coming. The פסוק uses the word 'מיץ' (pressing) three times. The next step will read it as a lesson about Torah learning, building on the theme of effort.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי ינאי
What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'For the pressing of milk brings out butter,'
phrases.notes: משלי ל:לג

phrases.english: 'and the pressing of the nose brings out blood,'
'and the pressing of anger brings out strife'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new דרשה on the theme of Torah learning, after the readings of 'הסכת' are finished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the פסוק in משלי ל:לג is teaching.

steps.title: The cream of Torah comes from working until it hurts
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the פסוק, about pressing milk into butter, is read as a lesson about great effort in Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: In whom do you find the 'butter' of Torah? In someone who throws up the milk he nursed from his mother's breasts over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the question from step 28. It explains the first phrase of the פסוק, 'pressing milk brings out butter.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Butter only comes from milk that is pressed and churned hard. In the same way, the richest part of Torah only comes to someone who pushes himself so hard that it is as if he throws up the very first milk he ever drank. This is a picture of total effort.

keyTerms.meaning: Butter or cream; here, the best and richest part of Torah

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a literal instruction. It is a strong picture meaning 'work at Torah with every ounce of strength you have.'

phrases.english: In whom do you find
the butter (cream) of Torah?
In one who throws up the milk
phrases.notes: A picture of working with all one's strength

phrases.english: that he nursed from his mother's breasts, over it (the Torah).

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא חֶמְאָה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first part of the question about the פסוק in משלי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'pressing milk brings out butter' teach?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The best of Torah is found in someone who works at it with total effort.

steps.title: Staying quiet once when the teacher is angry
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'pressing the nose (אף) brings out blood' teaches that a student who stays quiet the first time his רבי is angry will understand the laws of pure and impure blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And pressing the nose brings out blood': any student whose teacher gets angry at him the first time, and he stays quiet, will merit to tell apart impure blood from pure blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second phrase of the פסוק. It reads the word אף (nose) as also meaning anger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אף means both nose and anger. So the פסוק hints at a teacher's anger. A student who accepts it quietly is rewarded with 'blood,' which here means the hard laws of telling pure blood from impure blood (טהרה and טומאה).

keyTerms.meaning: To tell apart, to tell the difference
Impure blood and pure blood; a hard area of halacha

phrases.english: 'And pressing the nose brings out blood':
phrases.notes: The word אף means both 'nose' and 'anger.'

phrases.english: any student whose teacher gets angry at him
the first time, and he stays quiet
merits to tell apart
between impure blood and pure blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִיץ אַף יוֹצִיא דָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer, moving to the second phrase of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'pressing the nose brings out blood' teach?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A student who stays quiet once when his רבי is angry earns understanding of pure and impure blood.

steps.title: Staying quiet twice earns the deepest understanding
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'pressing anger (אפים) brings out strife' teaches that a student who stays quiet two times will understand the difference between דיני ממונות and דיני נפשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And pressing anger brings out strife': any student whose teacher gets angry at him the first and second time, and he stays quiet, will merit to tell apart money cases from life-and-death cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last phrase of the פסוק. The word אפים is plural, so it means the teacher got angry two times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אף means one anger, and אפים (plural) means two angers. Staying quiet twice is a higher level, so the reward is higher. 'Strife' (ריב) points to court cases, so the student gains the deep skill of telling apart דיני ממונות from דיני נפשות.

keyTerms.meaning: Plural of אף; here, two times of anger
Strife, a dispute; here, court cases

phrases.english: 'And pressing anger (plural) brings out strife':
any student whose teacher gets angry at him
the first time and the second time, and he stays quiet
phrases.notes: Two times, because אפים is plural

phrases.english: merits to tell apart
between money cases and life-and-death cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִיץ אַפַּיִם יוֹצִיא רִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 30. A double anger accepted quietly brings a higher reward.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'pressing anger brings out strife' teach?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A student who stays quiet twice earns understanding of דיני ממונות and דיני נפשות, the highest level.

steps.title: Proof that money law is the deepest area of Torah
steps.stepSummary: A משנה from רבי ישמעאל shows that דיני ממונות are the deepest area of Torah, so mastering them is the highest reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי ישמעאל says, one who wants to become wise should study money laws, because there is no area in Torah greater than them, since they are like a flowing spring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up step 31. It shows why understanding money cases is such a big reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might ask why money law is the top prize for staying quiet twice. רבי ישמעאל teaches that money law has no limit: new questions and ideas keep coming out of it like water from a spring. So it really is the highest level of learning.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
An area or subject of study
A flowing spring that never runs dry

steps.whatToRemember: The whole פסוק is read as a ladder: total effort brings the 'butter' of Torah. Staying quiet once under a רבי's anger brings understanding of blood laws. Staying quiet twice brings mastery of דיני ממונות, the deepest area of all.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Yishmael says:
One who wants to become wise
should study money laws,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לָךְ מִקְצוֹעַ בַּתּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מֵהֶן,
phrases.english: because there is no area in Torah greater than them,
since they are like a flowing spring.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 31 by showing that money law is the deepest area of Torah.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that understanding דיני ממונות is the highest reward.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה of רבי ישמעאל: there is no greater area of Torah than money law, which is like a flowing spring.

steps.title: Being willing to look foolish while learning leads to greatness
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains a פסוק: one who lowers himself to ask and learn will be raised up, and one who stays silent from embarrassment will end up unable to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: What does the פסוק mean, 'If you acted foolishly in lifting yourself up, or if you planned, put your hand over your mouth'? Anyone who makes himself look foolish for Torah will in the end be raised up. And if he muzzles himself, he will end with his hand over his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a new teaching on a nearby פסוק in משלי. It continues the theme of humility in learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'acted foolishly' as a person who does not mind looking foolish by asking questions, and 'lifting up' as his reward: he becomes great. He reads זמות as 'muzzled': a person who keeps quiet out of shame never learns, so later, when asked, he has to cover his mouth with nothing to say.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written
Acted foolishly / makes himself look foolish
In lifting up; here, being raised up
Hand over the mouth; having nothing to say

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict the earlier steps about staying quiet. Earlier, the student stays quiet when his רבי is angry (humility). Here, the problem is staying quiet out of embarrassment and not asking. Both teach humility.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'If you acted foolishly in lifting yourself up,
and if you planned (muzzled), put your hand over your mouth'?

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְנַבֵּל עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה —
phrases.english: Anyone who makes himself look foolish for words of Torah
will in the end be raised up.
And if he muzzles himself, his hand will be over his mouth.
phrases.notes: He will have no answer when asked

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching on the פסוק right before the earlier one, keeping the theme of humility in Torah learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who is willing to look foolish for Torah will be raised up. One who stays silent from embarrassment will end up with nothing to say.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: יתרו's descendants were spared, so a host of a תלמיד חכם earns even more
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה teaches from the פסוק about שאול and the קיני. יתרו was rewarded even though he was kind to משה for his own honor. So one who hosts a תלמיד חכם will certainly be rewarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה began in honor of the hosts and taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'And שאול said to the קיני: Go, leave, get away from among עמלק, so I do not destroy you with them, because you did kindness with all of Israel'? It is a קל וחומר. יתרו only brought משה close for his own honor, and still his family was protected. Someone who hosts a תלמיד חכם in his home, feeds him, gives him drink, and lets him use his things, will be rewarded all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the speeches of the חכמים at יבנה. רבי נחמיה gives a talk honoring the people who hosted them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קיני were descendants of יתרו, and שאול spared them because of the kindness יתרו did for Israel. יתרו's kindness was partly selfish, since he wanted the honor of having משה with him. If even that earned protection for his descendants, then hosting a תלמיד חכם for the sake of Torah earns much more.

keyTerms.meaning: He opened, meaning he began a public talk
In honor of the hosts (the people who hosted the חכמים)
An argument from a lighter case to a stronger case
The Kenite tribe, descendants of יתרו

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק talks about the קיני, but the lesson is about יתרו. The קיני were יתרו's descendants, so they were spared in his merit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya began (his talk)
in honor of the hosts, and expounded:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And Saul said to the Kenite:
Go, depart, get down
from among the Amalekites
lest I destroy you with them
for you did kindness
with all the Children of Israel"?
Isn't this a kal vachomer:
If Jethro
who brought Moses close
only for his own honor
is treated like this (rewarded),
then one who hosts a Torah scholar in his home,
and feeds him and gives him drink
and lets him benefit from his possessions
all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּתַח רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה בִּכְבוֹד אַכְסַנְיָא וְדָרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side teaching of רבי שמואל בר נחמני to the series of talks given by the חכמים at יבנה in honor of their hosts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If יתרו's self-interested kindness protected his descendants, hosting a תלמיד חכם certainly earns great reward.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: The מצרים earned gratitude, so a host of a תלמיד חכם earns even more
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי teaches from the מצוה not to hate a מצרי. The מצרים hosted Israel only for their own benefit, and still the Torah tells us to be grateful. So one who hosts a תלמיד חכם deserves much more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי began in honor of the hosts and taught: 'Do not hate an אדומי, for he is your brother. Do not hate a מצרי, for you were a stranger in his land.' It is a קל וחומר. The מצרים only brought Israel close for their own needs, as the פסוק says, 'If you know there are capable men among them, make them officers over my cattle.' Still, the Torah says not to hate them. Someone who hosts a תלמיד חכם, feeds him, gives him drink, and lets him use his things, deserves all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: A second חכם gives the same kind of talk in honor of the hosts, using a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרעה welcomed יוסף's family because he wanted skilled men to watch his cattle. That was selfish hosting, yet the Torah still demands gratitude to the מצרים. Hosting a תלמיד חכם without any personal gain must earn even greater thanks and reward.

keyTerms.meaning: An Edomite, a descendant of Esav

steps.confusionAlert: The מצרים later enslaved Israel. The point here is only that their first act of hosting, even though it was selfish, still created a debt of gratitude.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei began
in honor of the hosts, and expounded:
"Do not abhor an Edomite
for he is your brother;
do not abhor an Egyptian
for you were a stranger in his land."
Isn't this a kal vachomer:
If the Egyptians
who brought Israel close
only for their own needs,
as it says: "And if you know
that there are capable men among them,
then make them officers over the cattle
over what is mine"
are treated like this,
then one who hosts a Torah scholar in his home
and feeds him and gives him drink
and lets him benefit from his possessions
all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּתַח רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בִּכְבוֹד אַכְסַנְיָא וְדָרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel talk teaching the same lesson as רבי נחמיה, using a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the מצרים' selfish hosting earned Israel's gratitude, hosting a תלמיד חכם certainly earns more.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי: עובד אדום was blessed for the ארון, so a host earns even more
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי teaches from עובד אדום, who was blessed because the ארון stayed in his house. The ארון did not eat or drink, and he only swept and sprinkled water before it. So one who feeds and hosts a תלמיד חכם will surely be blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר, son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, began in honor of the hosts and taught: 'ה׳ blessed עובד אדום הגתי because of the Ark of God.' It is a קל וחומר. The ארון did not eat or drink. עובד אדום only swept and sprinkled water in front of it, and he was blessed. Someone who hosts a תלמיד חכם, feeds him, gives him drink, and lets him use his things, will be blessed all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: A third חכם gives the same kind of talk in honor of the hosts, this time using the story of the ארון in עובד אדום's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עובד אדום's service to the ארון was small: he cleaned the floor and settled the dust with water. He never had to feed it or give it drink. If that small honor brought a great blessing, then fully hosting a תלמיד חכם, who carries Torah like the ארון, brings even greater blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: עובד אדום from גת, in whose house the ארון stayed for three months
The Ark of God, which held the לוחות
Swept and sprinkled water to settle the dust

steps.whyThisMatters: This talk compares a תלמיד חכם to the ארון itself, because both carry Torah. That is why honoring him brings blessing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer began
son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
in honor of the hosts, and expounded:
"And the Lord blessed Oved Edom the Gittite
because of the Ark of God."
Isn't this a kal vachomer:
If for the Ark
which did not eat or drink,
but he only swept and sprinkled before it,
he was treated like this (blessed),
then one who hosts a Torah scholar in his home,
and feeds him and gives him drink
and lets him benefit from his possessions
all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּתַח רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי בִּכְבוֹד אַכְסַנְיָא וְדָרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third parallel talk in honor of the hosts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If small honor to the ארון brought blessing, hosting a תלמיד חכם certainly brings blessing.

steps.title: What was עובד אדום's blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what blessing עובד אדום actually received.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the blessing that ה׳ gave him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to fill in a detail about the last teaching. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only that עובד אדום was 'blessed' and does not say how. This is not a challenge to the teaching. The גמרא just wants to know what the reward looked like.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing with which He blessed him

phrases.english: What was the blessing with which He blessed him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִיא בְּרָכָה שֶׁבֵּרְכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a detail about the פסוק of עובד אדום quoted in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly was the blessing that עובד אדום received because of the ארון?

steps.title: רב יהודה בר זבידא: Many children born at once
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר זבידא answers that the blessing was children. חמות and her eight daughters-in-law each gave birth to six babies at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר זבידא said: This was חמות and her eight daughters-in-law, who each gave birth to six babies in one pregnancy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה בר זבידא answers the question. The blessing was a huge number of children in עובד אדום's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמות (עובד אדום's wife) and his eight daughters-in-law each had sextuplets. This shows how great the reward was for a small act of honor to the ארון. The sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of עובד אדום (the name חמות also means 'mother-in-law')
One womb, meaning a single pregnancy

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Zevida said:
This is Chamos and her eight daughters-in-law
who each gave birth to six
in a single womb (one pregnancy).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר זְבִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing was that עובד אדום's wife חמות and his eight daughters-in-law each gave birth to six children in one pregnancy.
